title: Penalty approach phase classification: independent methodology and failure audit
purpose: Research proposals and AI visual triage for the overnight optimization. This is not an annotation ground-truth file and must not silently override predictions.

baseline.other_28_identity_observation: Selected box appears to surround the kicker in the sampled panels. This does not establish every-frame track purity, contact timing, correct foot or step accuracy.
baseline.validation_scope: Existing validation checks frame bounds, source hash, field consistency, candidate count consistency and image decoding. It does not measure correct person or physical step accuracy.

user_feedback.interpretation: A genuine user-provided approximate clip-level assessment: about five steps, with four to six acceptable to this user for this example.
user_feedback.must_not_do: Do not turn this into exact five-step ground truth, a blanket plus/minus-one tolerance for every clip, or agreement-based proof of accuracy.

primary_sources.title: Design and Validation of an Observational System for Penalty Kick Analysis in Football (OSPAF)
primary_sources.verified_claim: An expert-validated observational framework treats penalty actions through explicit behavioral variables. Some initial variables, including run-up type and length, did not satisfy final validation requirements.
primary_sources.use_here: Use explicit observable definitions and observer agreement; do not claim that our new lateral, circling and acceleration labels are already validated by OSPAF.
primary_sources.code_provenance: Conceptual reference only; no code copied.

primary_sources.title: Body Pose Estimation Integrated With Notational Analysis: A New Approach to Analyze Penalty Kicks Strategy in Elite Football
primary_sources.verified_claim: Combines OpenPose and observational analysis. Table 1 separates approach speed, fluency, angle, steps and gaze. The study used a standardized rear view and found the selected shooter body angles did not significantly associate with shooter strategy.
primary_sources.use_here: Separate observable movement descriptors from inferred decision strategy; do not infer keeper dependence from a stutter or curved approach alone. Do not transfer its reported accuracy to this project.
primary_sources.code_provenance: Conceptual reference only; current repository uses YOLO pose, not the paper's OpenPose pipeline.

primary_sources.title: Ultralytics pose task documentation
primary_sources.verified_claim: Pose inference outputs keypoint coordinates and confidence values; standard COCO pose has 17 landmarks.
primary_sources.use_here: COCO ankles do not include heel/toe contact geometry. A keypoint confidence value is not a calibrated probability that a real physical landing occurred.
primary_sources.code_provenance: Existing project calls the Ultralytics pretrained model API; phase logic and event heuristics are project-specific.

primary_sources.title: OpenCV: Basic concepts of the homography explained with code
primary_sources.verified_claim: A planar homography relates points between planes and supports perspective correction.
primary_sources.use_here: Only calibrated ground-plane locations can justify field direction, distance and curvature. Mapping hips, airborne feet or an airborne ball with a pitch homography does not recover their true ground position or 3D trajectory.
primary_sources.code_provenance: API/concept reference, not proof that calibration has been implemented or independently validated for these clips.

primary_sources.title: OpenCV: estimateAffinePartial2D
primary_sources.verified_claim: estimateAffinePartial2D estimates a limited four-degree-of-freedom 2D affine transform and returns inlier information; RANSAC is supported.
primary_sources.use_here: Fit background motion with people excluded; report inlier counts and residual error, and abstain when stabilization fails. Similarity compensation is not full pitch calibration.
primary_sources.code_provenance: Proposed use of an official API; project-specific gating thresholds would need validation.

primary_sources.title: BoT-SORT: Robust Associations Multi-Pedestrian Tracking
primary_sources.verified_claim: Combines motion and appearance information with camera-motion compensation for multi-person tracking.
primary_sources.use_here: Motivates identity continuity and camera compensation. It does not by itself identify the penalty taker or label physical foot contacts.
primary_sources.code_provenance: Design reference only; existing nearest-centre tracker is not BoT-SORT.

primary_sources.title: SciPy find_peaks documentation
primary_sources.verified_claim: find_peaks finds local maxima and filters by properties such as distance and prominence; noise can change peak positions.
primary_sources.use_here: Signal extrema are event candidates, not biomechanical proof of foot landing. Smoothing and thresholds require sensitivity tests.
primary_sources.code_provenance: Existing project uses this library function; physical interpretation of its peaks is our heuristic.

primary_sources.title: SoccerNet Game State Reconstruction
primary_sources.verified_claim: The task distinguishes player, goalkeeper, referee and other roles alongside tracking and field localization.
primary_sources.use_here: Person detection and tracking are not role recognition. The current wrong-kicker failures require role or ball-interaction evidence before phase classification.
primary_sources.code_provenance: Task-level architectural analogy only; no SoccerNet code copying or trained role classifier is established.

primary_sources.title: SoccerNet Camera Calibration
primary_sources.verified_claim: Camera parameters are assessed through reprojection error against pitch geometry.
primary_sources.use_here: A visually plausible top-down rendering alone is insufficient calibration QA; use landmark or line reprojection evidence.

recommended_operational_model.principle: Describe what happens in each clip; do not diagnose a player's enduring penalty strategy or intentions from one or two examples.
separate_axes: trajectory shape relative to a declared coordinate frame

phases.label: preparation_adjustment
phases.definition: Visible pre-approach movement that has not yet begun the sustained progression ending at the strike. This may include lateral repositioning, stepping in place or retreating to set the approach.
phases.boundary_evidence: Identity-consistent body/ground path relative to ball or approach axis, followed by the continuous approach episode; speed alone is insufficient.
phases.step_policy: Report preparation contact candidates separately. Do not delete them or call them errors simply because displacement is small.

phases.label: committed_approach
phases.definition: The progression episode toward the ball that culminates in the strike, including short strides and internal hesitations.
phases.boundary_evidence: Progress over a sustained window and connection to an independently supported contact candidate; preserve approach before an internal pause.
phases.step_policy: Count all supported contacts in this phase, including short strides. Keep their size/tempo attributes separate.

phases.label: strike_transition
phases.definition: A short interval containing final plant, kicking-leg swing and ball-contact candidate rather than an overconfident single-frame truth.
phases.boundary_evidence: Foot-ball proximity plus ball departure where available, supported by body/foot motion. If only pose is present, label the strike as uncertain.
phases.step_policy: Final support-foot landing may be a step; foot-ball impact itself and airborne swing extrema are not additional ground contacts.

phases.label: post_strike_recovery
phases.definition: Movement after the supported strike interval, including balance recovery, follow-through, walking and celebration.
phases.step_policy: Exclude from the approach count, retain optional recovery events separately.

phases.label: unknown_or_not_observable
phases.definition: Identity, boundary, motion compensation or visibility is insufficient; do not force a category.
phases.step_policy: Missing preparation is not zero preparation; a left-censored approach count is a visible lower bound, not the complete count.

motion_attributes.label: lateral_adjustment_candidate
motion_attributes.definition: Motion predominantly perpendicular to the estimated final approach direction, with limited forward progress, before the approach episode.
motion_attributes.avoid: Do not equate screen-left/screen-right motion with sidestepping in field coordinates or body-relative side-stepping.

motion_attributes.label: curved_approach_candidate
motion_attributes.definition: Smoothed trajectory direction changes consistently while making net progress toward the contact area.
motion_attributes.avoid: A curved trajectory is not automatically a full circle, and the curvature may be image-projection or camera error.

motion_attributes.label: loop_like_adjustment_candidate
motion_attributes.definition: A sustained same-signed turn with appreciable angular sweep and return/closure relative to path length, before final progression.
motion_attributes.avoid: Do not assign this from one noisy bend, low-motion jitter or a camera pan. Exact circle/metric curvature requires a supported coordinate model.

motion_attributes.label: short_accelerating_onset_candidate
motion_attributes.definition: Several small displacement events accompanied by increasing smoothed progression speed before the faster final approach.
motion_attributes.avoid: Do not automatically remove these events from the approach count; phase membership depends on when progression starts.

motion_attributes.label: fast_final_approach_candidate
motion_attributes.definition: Relatively faster forward progression in the later pre-contact part of the same clip.
motion_attributes.avoid: Without metric ground speed and a prespecified sprint criterion, do not label an absolute sprint or report m/s.

motion_attributes.label: pause_or_stutter_candidate
motion_attributes.definition: A persistent low-progress interval between two moving intervals, or short cadence changes within the approach episode.
motion_attributes.avoid: Do not restart the entire approach after every pause; do not infer psychological deception or keeper dependence.

coordinate_rules.image_only: Output apparent image-space motion or body-height-normalized motion per second. State that perspective, body posture and residual camera motion remain confounders.
coordinate_rules.camera_compensated: Estimate transforms from stable background features excluding all person boxes. Retain transform QC and reset at cuts. Low inliers or large residuals require unknown, not aggressive interpolation.
coordinate_rules.calibrated_pitch: Metric path, field-relative direction and speed require verified pitch geometry, scale and reprojection accuracy. Use estimated ground contacts, not hip coordinates directly.
coordinate_rules.body_relative: Left/right body-relative sidestepping requires reliable body orientation and anatomical left/right identity; do not infer it from screen direction.

recommended_operational_model.count_definition: A step is a new observable ground-contact event after foot transfer; initially planted feet and shot impact alone are not new steps. A signal maximum/minimum remains only a candidate until foot-contact evidence supports it.
recommended_operational_model.uncertainty_model: Store identity confidence, contact timing uncertainty, visibility, stabilization quality and event reliability separately. Do not compress all uncertainty into one uncalibrated number called accuracy.
recommended_operational_model.classification_format: Allow multiple attributes per phase and multiple phases per clip; reserve unknown. Do not force every player into one exclusive named technique.

code_audit.finding: The filtered candidates list is populated using outlier, lead-time and approach-displacement constraints, but is not used to select the returned frame. The function chooses the largest eligible ankle burst before 82 percent of shot duration, with a 55-to-75 percent central fallback.
code_audit.consequence: A burst caused by a goalkeeper, referee, keypoint jitter or post-contact motion can be emitted as a kick. Shot-length percentages encode editing convention, not physical contact evidence.
code_audit.proposal: Use independent ball proximity/departure or explicit pose-only uncertainty and compare candidate alternatives; guard by tracked role. Never silently treat maximum ankle displacement as confirmed ball contact.

code_audit.finding: Adequate pose coverage and substantial generic lower-body motion qualify a person. No ball interaction or player/goalkeeper/referee role test is required.
code_audit.consequence: The goalkeeper's jump and leg motion can outrank the kicker, while a continuously visible referee can also qualify.
code_audit.proposal: Establish who approaches and interacts with the ball, with geometry/role and identity evidence. If no candidate is sufficiently supported, abstain or request review instead of force-selecting.

code_audit.finding: first_viable stops at the first shot with any qualified track. A full-body goalkeeper in a front view may satisfy that criterion before the true approach shot.
code_audit.consequence: The repaired shot selector can still stop on a wrong role or incomplete approach, although it no longer blindly stops at the first cut.
code_audit.proposal: Qualify the actual action sequence and visible pre-contact span, not merely a generic moving full-body person; retain competing shots and reasons.

code_audit.finding: Motion onset uses uncorrected image hip displacement divided by body-box height and frame gap. It takes the first short stationary-to-motion transition and adds preroll.
code_audit.consequence: Camera motion, posture noise or preparatory shifts can trigger an early onset, while true pauses and first-step definition remain conflated.
code_audit.proposal: Use camera QC, directional progress, minimum dwell and phase hysteresis; preserve preparatory events separately. Evaluate boundary ambiguity rather than picking a threshold to make counts look plausible.

code_audit.finding: Validation is structural and correctly disclaims accuracy, but the public count of 39 successful extractions can be misread as 39 successful kicker identifications.
code_audit.proposal: Report separate decoding completeness, candidate-output availability, correct-identity audit, contact-boundary audit, phase usability and verified count accuracy denominators.

ai_visual_audit.basis: All 39 existing yellow-box QA JPG contact sheets were opened and inspected, not every video frame. Frame IDs below are zero-based original-clip IDs shown on those sheets.

ablation_protocol.purpose: Separate improvements in selection, timing, phase definition and event detection instead of judging a bundle only by how many numeric outputs it produces.
ablation_protocol.baseline_policy: Keep original clips and the repaired baseline read-only. Save configuration, dependency versions, source hashes and absolute source-frame coordinates per run.

stages.evaluate: 39-output structural checks plus the 11 known AI-observed wrong-identity examples; no accuracy claim.
Which of the 11 wrong-person cases are corrected or responsibly abstained on? Check previously plausible examples for new identity regressions. Keep step detector fixed.

stages.change: Contact timing only on identity-supported tracks
stages.evaluate: For Ramos/Bacca/Schone/Aspas, compare both timing and neighboring frames. Keep counts provisional. Report timing-error metrics only after actual independent reference frames or intervals exist.
Compare raw versus stabilized paths, residual QC and prep/approach/recovery membership on the same tracks. Report disagreement/coverage, not accuracy, until reviewed.
Check final support foot, initial planted foot, same-foot candidates, gaps and post-contact leakage. Count genuine short steps within approach rather than deleting all small steps.
Assess whether curve, lateral and acceleration labels are stable across smoothing windows and thresholds; low-stability cases become uncertain.

ablation_protocol.parameter_sensitivity: Vary smoothing window, onset dwell, minimum contact separation and contact-boundary uncertainty independently; report changed decisions and count range. All chosen numeric thresholds are engineering hypotheses, not sports-science constants.
evaluation_units: Selected person role and identity continuity
Contact/onset boundary error or agreement intervals
Event precision/recall with prespecified one-to-one temporal matching tolerance after event labels exist
Phase duration/temporal overlap and categorical agreement after phase labels exist
Exact count error and any explicitly approved approximate tolerance
Abstention/unknown rate alongside error among accepted outputs
ablation_protocol.review_design: Show original unannotated video first for independent count and boundary judgments, then reveal overlays for disagreement analysis. Record reviewer, date, definition and uncertainty. AI triage may prioritize cases but must remain separated from human annotations.
ablation_protocol.split_policy: Do not choose thresholds by repeatedly fitting these 39 clips and present the same clips as an independent test. Group by match/shootout and player when constructing any tune/test protocol, and state generalization claims modestly.
morning_acceptance: Review player identity and a contact-time thumbnail before reading the number.
See separate preparation, approach and recovery candidates with absolute-frame evidence.
See unknown or partial-visibility labels when appropriate rather than invented full counts.
Preserve the Cuadrado user assessment as approximate, case-specific feedback.
Provide representative original-video/overlay pairs and a complete 39-clip manifest without implying 39 validated outcomes.

defensible_teacher_explanation.method: A transparent, phase-aware computer-vision prototype combines pretrained pose coordinates, identity/shot evidence, camera-motion checks and explicit temporal rules. It reports observable approach characteristics, not hidden intent.
main_weaknesses_beyond_sample_size: Role confusion: person pose does not establish who is the kicker.
Circular timing: using the strongest leg motion to define both the kick and the counting window can validate its own mistake.
Construct validity: a pose extremum is not necessarily ground contact; small preparation steps and short approach steps need an agreed definition.
Coordinate validity: pixel speed and curvature mix perspective, zoom and camera motion.
Truncation: missing prelude or run-up is not zero motion; incomplete visibility requires partial/unknown output.
Validation: reproducible code, successful decoding and warning-free outputs are distinct from independent accuracy evidence.
Threshold tuning: hardcoded shot fractions and per-clip adjustments may overfit broadcast editing.
Strategy interpretation: motion, gaze and interaction timing are different observables; no mind-reading or enduring player labels.
